opening.argument: The video describes a direct action-for-money pathway: after an apparent Apple-support contact claimed he could fix the MacBook for a fee, the viewer was told to buy gift cards. The requested purchase was therefore tied to a promised technical outcome, and the account says $800 worth of cards were ultimately given. That is a concrete solicitation involving an easy-to-transfer asset, presented through an apparent support identity and an urgent device problem. The fact that the payment was requested as gift cards strengthens the concern because the requested action was clearly connected to obtaining the promised fix.
